issues.description: NEVRA-to-path assumes filename starts with a letter; numeric-prefixed packages will break
issues.detail: `nevra[0].lower()` is used to construct the koji subdirectory (e.g. `/p/python3-foo-...rpm`). Koji's canonical layout uses the first character of the package name. If any package filename begins with a digit (e.g. `389-ds-base-...rpm`, `3proxy-...rpm`), the constructed URL points to `/3/...` which may or may not match the actual koji layout, and `.lower()` on a digit is a no-op masking the assumption. The data structure here (raw filename string) is fighting the algorithm — parse the NEVRA into a struct (name, version, release, arch) once and let the path fall out of it.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returns None silently; caller doesn't check
issues.detail: If `extract_arch_from_url` finds no match it returns `None`, and the caller immediately does `koji_url_base + f"/latest/{arch}/Packages"` producing `.../latest/None/Packages/...`. That's a 404 surfaced far from the cause. Either raise on no-match or have the caller assert. The data flow should not permit a `None` to be silently formatted into a URL string.

issues.description: Regex compiled per-call inside a loop
issues.detail: `extract_arch_from_url` recompiles the same regex on every URL. The arch list is static — compile once at module scope. Minor, but lifting the constant out also makes the data (the supported arches) visible at the top of the file where it belongs.

issues.description: Arch list duplicated as implicit knowledge
issues.detail: The supported arches `['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x']` live as a literal inside `extract_arch_from_url`. The rest of the program also iterates arches (via `generate_main`). Pick one place for that list — a module-level constant — so the data has one home. Right now the same fact is encoded in two places.

issues.description: Regex is overkill for a path-segment match
issues.detail: A URL is already `/`-delimited. Splitting on `/` and checking set membership against the arch list is shorter, has no regex-escape concerns, and makes the data shape (path segments) explicit. Classic case where picking the right data structure (list of path segments) makes the algorithm obvious and the regex disappears.

issues.description: use_koji_url_only is a filter — say so in the shape
issues.detail: This function is a stateless transform: list of URLs in, list of URLs out. Good. But the inner loop mixes two concerns: pass-through for coreos-pool URLs, and rewrite for others. Splitting into `is_coreos_pool(url)` and `rewrite_to_coreos_pool(url)` and using a list comprehension makes the filter shape obvious and each piece independently testable. Small thing; it earns its keep here because the rewrite logic is the part that can go wrong.

review.summary: The change is small, the shape is right — a stateless filter from URL list to URL list — and removing the dnf5 workaround in favor of constructing canonical koji paths is the simpler design. The data structures, however, are doing less work than they could: NEVRA is kept as a raw filename string and arch is extracted by regex from a URL that's already path-delimited, which leaves two silent failure modes (None arch formatted into a URL; first-char-of-filename assumed alphabetic). Parse the NEVRA once into a small struct and lift the arch list to a module constant; the rewrite then becomes self-evident and the regex goes away. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE in shape, WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE in the details.
